patch.value: The changelog heading records the day it was generated, so the gate fails every following day

Two clock dependencies in the release gate. The lockfile pinned a pm-changelog older than 2026.8.2, which derived release dates in local time, so a host at a positive UTC offset and a UTC runner disagreed about the date. The one that actually bit this package: it is release-gated and therefore has no tags, and without a tag pm-changelog falls back to the current date for the release heading. The committed heading recorded the day it happened to be generated rather than the date the version encodes, so changelog:check compared against a freshly generated heading and failed on every subsequent day. The check was already failing when this was found, with no change to the tracker or the code. Every released package in this fleet pairs a CalVer version with its matching date, so the generated heading was inconsistent with that convention as well as unstable.

The lockfile resolves pm-changelog to 2026.8.2 or newer; the three changelog scripts pass an explicit release date rather than relying on the fallback; the committed heading pairs the version with the date that version encodes; changelog:check passes today and passes again under a timezone a day behind this host, so its result does not depend on when it runs
Pinned --date 2026-07-31 across changelog, changelog:full and changelog:check, corrected the committed heading to 2026.7.31 - 2026-07-31, and refreshed the lockfile onto pm-changelog 2026.8.3.
changelog:check produces the same verdict on any day and in any timezone, rather than agreeing only on the day the file was generated.
changelog:check passes, and passes again under TZ=Etc/GMT+12 which is a day behind this host. Before the fix the check was already failing, having been generated on a previous day.

The three changelog scripts now pass an explicit release date instead of relying on the untagged fallback, the committed heading pairs the version with the date that version encodes, and the lockfile resolves pm-changelog 2026.8.3. changelog:check passes, and passes again under TZ=Etc/GMT+12, so its result no longer depends on when or where it runs.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Release-time caveat. The --date 2026-07-31 pin is an unconditional override, not a fallback, because pm-changelog has no fallback-shaped flag today. It is correct while this package is unreleased and untagged, but the moment a real release tag exists it will win over that tag's own date. Removing the three pins is part of cutting the first release, not an optional cleanup. Filed upstream on pm-changelog as issue 120.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Applied the same end-to-end correction found on the pm-vcs review: release:notes invoked pm-changelog without --date while changelog:check used the pinned one, so the gate and the release body it gates could have disagreed about the date. All four invocations now carry --date 2026-07-31.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Third and final set of invocation sites. The release workflow does not call the npm scripts; it spells the pm-changelog command out again in three run steps, so pinning the four package.json scripts left those three unpinned and the claim of one release-date source was still false. All seven sites in this package now carry --date 2026-07-31. The underlying cause is the duplication itself: the same command exists in seven places with slightly different flags, so any per-site fix has to be repeated seven times and silently rots when one is missed. The durable fix is for the workflow to invoke the npm scripts rather than restate them, which would leave exactly one place to pin and one place to unpin when the release gate is lifted. Not done here because changing the release path of a gated package is a larger change than the defect being fixed, and the workflow steps differ from the scripts in --pm-bin and in redirecting to RELEASE_NOTES.md rather than the step summary.
